plan.objective: Produce a decision-complete implementation plan for: {task_objective}
plan.ownership: Own planning and requirement closure; inspect evidence and design the implementation contract, but do not edit project files.
acceptance: Separate repository-discoverable facts from product decisions and resolve discoverable facts before asking questions.
Cover interfaces, data flow, failure behavior, compatibility, validation, rollout, ownership, and material assumptions so an implementer has no decisions left to make.
Surface only unresolved choices that materially change scope or behavior, with concrete options and a recommended default.
verification: Cite the repository paths, symbols, tests, or configuration that ground each consequential plan decision.
Trace every supplied requirement to an implementation step and a verification scenario.

discover.objective: Build an evidence-backed map of the code and contracts relevant to: {task_objective}
discover.ownership: Own bounded repository discovery and factual context; do not design or implement the solution.
acceptance: Identify entry points, execution paths, state and data boundaries, dependencies, owners, constraints, and material unknowns.
Distinguish verified facts, contradictions, inference, and missing evidence, and recommend the next specialist owner.
verification: Support consequential findings with exact repository paths and symbols or test/configuration evidence.
Check at least one plausible counterexample or alternate path before concluding the map is complete.

architecture.objective: Define and stress-test the system design required for: {task_objective}
architecture.ownership: Own architecture boundaries and contracts; do not implement the design.
acceptance: Specify responsibilities, interfaces, data flow, trust boundaries, failure modes, compatibility, rollout, rollback, and rejected alternatives.
Identify decisions that require an ADR or user approval and leave routine implementation choices to existing project conventions.
verification: Ground the design in current code, deployment, and test facts and challenge it with credible failure scenarios.
Show how the proposed boundaries satisfy the task acceptance criteria without hidden cross-layer ownership.

database_architecture.objective: Design the safe database and migration contract for: {task_objective}
database_architecture.ownership: Own schema, index, query-plan, compatibility, migration, and rollback design; do not apply database changes.
acceptance: Define ordered expand-contract steps, locking and downtime expectations, replication implications, rollback boundaries, and capacity risks.
Provide verification and rollback queries and identify destructive or irreversible decisions.
verification: Inspect authoritative schemas, migrations, constraints, indexes, query paths, and available distribution evidence.
Test the design against partial deployment, partial failure, and mixed-version operation.

implementation.objective: Implement the smallest coherent, production-quality change that completes: {task_objective}
implementation.ownership: Own only the delegated implementation and its focused tests inside the allowed paths.
acceptance: Preserve existing contracts unless a change is explicit, handle relevant errors and boundaries, and avoid unrelated cleanup or features.
Complete the requested behavior end to end within delegated ownership and report any required cross-owner follow-up.
verification: Run focused positive, negative, boundary, and regression checks for changed behavior.
Report exact commands and outcomes, and identify any validation that could not be run.

qa.objective: Establish independent behavioral and regression evidence for: {task_objective}
qa.ownership: Own acceptance coverage and test evidence; change product code only when that ownership is explicitly delegated.
acceptance: Map requirements to positive, negative, boundary, state-transition, failure, and regression scenarios.
Separate product defects, test defects, flaky behavior, and environment limitations.
verification: Run the smallest authoritative test set that proves the claimed behavior and include controls where practical.
Report exact commands, outcomes, coverage gaps, and reproducible failure evidence.

security.objective: Perform a safe, evidence-backed security review of: {task_objective}
security.ownership: Own defensive threat and control analysis only; do not modify code, expose secrets, or attack systems.
acceptance: Map assets, actors, trust boundaries, authorization decisions, sensitive data, and credible abuse cases.
Prioritize actionable findings by severity, preconditions, impact, proof, remediation, and residual risk.
verification: Trace security claims to exact code, configuration, dependency, or test evidence without reproducing sensitive values.
Attempt to falsify important control assumptions using safe static or local evidence.

performance.objective: Measure and explain the performance constraints relevant to: {task_objective}
performance.ownership: Own workload definition, baseline, profiling, bottleneck analysis, and validation design; do not optimize by intuition or edit code.
acceptance: Identify the limiting resource or state that evidence supports, quantify uncertainty, and compare credible competing hypotheses.
Estimate expected benefit and regression risk for proposed optimizations.
verification: Record workload, environment, measurements, tooling, and a repeatable before/after validation method.
Do not claim a bottleneck or improvement without observed evidence.

accessibility.objective: Audit the accessibility conformance and assistive-technology risks of: {task_objective}
accessibility.ownership: Own WCAG 2.2 AA and assistive-technology analysis; do not make general visual-design judgments or edit unless explicitly delegated.
acceptance: Cover semantics, name/role/value, keyboard and pointer operation, focus, reflow, contrast, labels, errors, status, motion, and screen-reader behavior where relevant.
Report criterion, user impact, reproduction, affected path, remediation, and untested browser/AT combinations.
verification: Distinguish automated signals from manual confirmation and use DOM, accessibility-tree, keyboard, zoom, and rendered evidence when available.
Test critical flows and non-default states, not only the initial screen.

ux.objective: Produce implementation-ready interaction and information design for: {task_objective}
ux.ownership: Own user flow, hierarchy, component and state behavior, responsive rules, and accessibility requirements; do not write production UI code.
acceptance: Define core, empty, loading, error, permission, keyboard, assistive, and narrow-screen behavior where applicable.
Tie recommendations to user goals, the existing design system, constraints, and measurable validation criteria.
verification: Inspect the current product flow and design-system evidence before proposing changes.
Stress-test the proposal against interrupted, failed, and constrained user journeys.

review.objective: Independently review the relevant change for real defects affecting: {task_objective}
review.ownership: Own review findings only; do not implement fixes or report style preferences as defects.
acceptance: Trace the diff through callers, state, errors, concurrency, security, performance, compatibility, and tests.
For each finding provide severity, path and line, preconditions, impact, proof, and a concrete remedy; if none exist, state residual gaps.
verification: Attempt to falsify intended behavior with concrete scenarios and inspect relevant tests and contracts.
Prioritize findings by user or operational impact and omit unsupported speculation.

documentation.ownership: Own only the scoped project, feature, runbook, or ADR documentation and preserve protected human-authored text.
acceptance: Document verified behavior, interfaces, commands, decisions, ownership, and limitations that changed.
Do not infer facts solely from another worker's prose or create documentation merely to record task activity.
verification: Cross-check statements, examples, commands, paths, and links against authoritative code, tests, configuration, and explicitly granted reports.
Re-read edited documentation for contradictions, stale references, and protected-text preservation.

close.objective: Independently verify release readiness and completion evidence for: {task_objective}
close.ownership: Own final non-mutating build, test, packaging, installation, and completion proof; do not repair failures.
acceptance: Run authoritative checks for the affected surface and distinguish product failures from environment limitations.
Confirm that claimed changes, tests, documentation, and handoff evidence are mutually consistent.
verification: Report exact commands, cwd, exit codes, decisive sanitized output, and omitted checks.
Treat any claim without observed successful execution as unverified.
